stage_name: Stabilize tests and make capabilities truthful
note_on_commits: No new commit was created. Per Git safety protocol, commits are only made on explicit user request. All S1 work is present as uncommitted working-tree changes on top of the S0 baseline commit.
changed_files: README.md (pre-existing uncommitted change from before S0, unrelated to S1)
frozen_decisions_applied: FD-11 Capability truthfulness: temporary source booleans removed; Zigbee/MQTT/Matter/OTA/RCP availability now comes from a build/runtime capability contract (service::RuntimeCapabilities), computed once at the composition root from Kconfig/HAL truth sources.

Plan Section 7.5 / INV-CONC-01 precursor: no pointer/reference into a ServiceRuntime::state() snapshot may outlive the temporary — all 3 known violations fixed, plus a full-repository audit found no other instances in tests or production code.
S1 required change #7: capabilities DTO/service projection defined and tested this stage; public /api/v1/capabilities route registration is explicitly deferred to S4 per the plan and was NOT added.

1_dangling_pointer_fix.root_cause: test/host/test_service_reporting_{stale,semantics,faults}.cpp called find_device()/find_online_device() with `runtime.state()` passed inline as an argument. ServiceRuntime::state() returns core::CoreState by value; the temporary is destroyed at the end of the full expression, so the returned pointer aliased freed stack storage on every subsequent dereference (ASan: stack-use-after-scope).
1_dangling_pointer_fix.fix: Every inline `find_*(runtime.state(), addr)` call site was rewritten to first bind the snapshot to a named local (`core::CoreState state = runtime.state();` or a per-block named local), matching the pattern already used correctly elsewhere in the same files, then pass that named local to the finder function.
1_dangling_pointer_fix.audit_scope: Grepped every `.state()`/`.snapshot()` call site across test/, components/, main/. All other occurrences either bind to a named local already, read a scalar member value immediately within the same expression (no pointer/reference stored), or (one case, test_service_hal_adapter.cpp) use a range-based for loop over a temporary's member, which is standards-safe because reference-binding a temporary's subobject in the range-for's implicit `auto&&` extends the complete temporary's lifetime for the loop's duration. Production adapters (MatterBridge/MqttBridge sync_runtime_snapshot) write into a persistent member cache via an out-parameter, not a temporary — no bug there.
1_dangling_pointer_fix.verification: All 3 previously-failing tests now PASS under ASan+UBSan; full host suite is 70/70 (69 pre-existing + 1 new) under both normal and sanitizer builds, with 0 sanitizer failures (previously 66/69).

2_ktemporarilydisable_removal.inventory: Exactly 8 occurrence lines / 4 declarations found, matching the plan's stated reviewed count exactly.
declarations_removed: main/app_main.cpp: kTemporarilyDisableMqttForWifiBootSanity (was false; dead weight above the already-working CONFIG_ZGW_MQTT_TRANSPORT_ENABLED gate in hal_mqtt_init())
main/app_main.cpp: kTemporarilyDisableMatterForWifiBootSanity (was false; redundant wrapper around the already-truthful hal_matter_available() weak-symbol check)

main/app_main.cpp: kTemporarilyDisableZigbeeForOtaRfIsolation (was TRUE — an active production bug: introduced 2026-03-28 for a one-off OTA RF isolation HIL test and left enabled ever since, meaning every boot since that commit had Zigbee completely disabled)
components/service/service_runtime.cpp: kTemporarilyDisableRcpWorkerForZigbeeIsolation (was true; RCP worker task was unconditionally never started)
2_ktemporarilydisable_removal.replacement: All four now read service::RuntimeCapabilities fields instead: caps.mqtt_available, caps.matter_target_available, caps.zigbee_available (app_main.cpp), capabilities_.rcp_update_available (service_runtime.cpp).
2_ktemporarilydisable_removal.new_kconfig_symbol: ZGW_ZIGBEE_ENABLED (bool, default y) added to main/Kconfig.projbuild. This is the functional fix for the shipped-disabled-Zigbee bug: normal/production builds now enable Zigbee by default; an explicit RF-isolation/dev build can still set it to n via the standard Kconfig/sdkconfig override mechanism, with no dedicated profile file needed.
2_ktemporarilydisable_removal.existing_kconfig_reused: CONFIG_ZGW_MQTT_TRANSPORT_ENABLED, CONFIG_ZGW_OTA_ENABLED, CONFIG_ZGW_RCP_TARGET_BACKEND_UART, and the hal_matter_available() weak-symbol probe were already real, working truth sources; S1 wired the composition root's capability computation to consult them directly instead of duplicating gates.

3_runtime_capabilities_contract.shape: struct RuntimeCapabilities { bool zigbee_available, mqtt_available, matter_target_available, ota_available, rcp_update_available; } — all default-false (unset capability is never assumed available).
3_runtime_capabilities_contract.ownership: Pure data, zero ESP-IDF dependency (INV-ARCH-01 preserved). ServiceRuntimeApi gained set_capabilities()/capabilities() pure-virtual pair; ServiceRuntime is the sole implementer (verified no other class implements the interface, so adding pure virtuals was safe).
3_runtime_capabilities_contract.injection_point: main/app_main.cpp computes the real values from Kconfig macros and hal_matter_available() at the very start of app_main(), before initialize_hal_adapter() and before start(), then calls g_runtime.set_capabilities(caps). Adapters/UI do not query Kconfig or HAL weak symbols directly — they must consult the service-owned projection (matches plan's 'capability availability is a service-owned read model').
3_runtime_capabilities_contract.thread_safety: New dedicated capabilities_lock_ (RuntimeLock, same primitive as the existing ingress_lock_/worker_start_lock_) guards a plain capabilities_ member; set/get both take the lock.
3_runtime_capabilities_contract.tests: test/host/test_service_capabilities.cpp: verifies all-false defaults, full replace-not-merge semantics on set_capabilities(), and read-back correctness.
3_runtime_capabilities_contract.deferred_to_s4: The public GET /api/v1/capabilities HTTP route and its JSON DTO/serializer are explicitly NOT added in S1, per the plan's instruction that only the DTO/service projection needs to be defined and tested in S1 while the public route is registered in S4 alongside the rest of the v1 API surface.

4_sanitizer_ci_gate.added: .github/workflows/ci.yml: new `sanitizer-tests` job ('Host Unit Tests (ASan+UBSan, Blocking)'), runs on push/pull_request, blocking (no `continue-on-error`), builds test/host with -fsanitize=address,undefined and runs the full ctest suite with ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=1 UBSAN_OPTIONS=print_stacktrace=1.
4_sanitizer_ci_gate.rationale: The pre-existing `reporting-regression` job already exercised the 3 affected tests but WITHOUT sanitizer flags, so it could never have caught the dangling-pointer class of bug. This gap is now closed.

5_architecture_gate_rule.added: check_arch_invariants.sh: new rule INV-H004 (high severity) using the existing check_absent helper, scanning components/ and main/ for the literal `kTemporarilyDisable` pattern.
5_architecture_gate_rule.verified_working: Manually appended a `kTemporarilyDisableTestProbe` comment to service_runtime.cpp and re-ran the gate: it correctly reported a HIGH violation and FAILED. Confirmed the rule is not a no-op before relying on it.

incident.what_happened: While verifying the new INV-H004 rule actually detects violations, a temporary probe line was appended to components/service/service_runtime.cpp and then reverted with `git checkout -- components/service/service_runtime.cpp`. Because that file already had uncommitted S1 changes (RuntimeCapabilities set_capabilities/capabilities implementation and the RCP worker gate replacement) that were never committed, `git checkout --` restored the ENTIRE file to the last commit (800fe93), silently discarding both real S1 edits along with the probe line — a violation of the safety protocol requirement to check git status/diff before any command that can discard uncommitted work.
incident.detection: Immediately re-grepped the file for the expected set_capabilities/capabilities_ symbols after the revert; found them missing and kTemporarilyDisableRcpWorkerForZigbeeIsolation back in place.
incident.impact: Contained to exactly one file (git diff --stat confirmed no other file was touched by the checkout). No data outside this session's own uncommitted work was at risk (nothing had been pushed or committed).
incident.recovery: Reapplied both edits to components/service/service_runtime.cpp from memory of the original diff (removal of the kTemporarilyDisableRcpWorkerForZigbeeIsolation declaration, replacement of its usage with capabilities_.rcp_update_available, and re-addition of the set_capabilities()/capabilities() method bodies), then reran the full architecture gate + host + integration + sanitizer suite to confirm the recovered state is identical in behavior to the pre-incident state.
incident.outcome: Fully recovered; all 4 verification suites green after recovery (see tests_and_checks below).
